findings: The opt-in core trace now exposes per-firing drive and modulatory provenance, typed causal-origin resolution, typed return-origin evaluation, and typed reverse-path evaluation through ordinary public Rust enums.

The public physical_diagnostics iterator is a pure projection of the existing trace; tracing-disabled runs remain empty, traced and untraced behavior remains equal, and traced checkpoint replay remains exact.
A two-origin incidence reports both physical origins and reports JunctionFallback with the receiving junction physical identity; a one-origin incidence reports Preserved.

Return decisions distinguish direct and local admission, remembered and same-moment duplicates, missing or inactive edges and endpoints, absent origins, and measured non-local rejection without changing the existing admission result.
Every existing reverse-consolidation early return now emits one typed terminal reason, while success emits Consolidated and retains the existing ReversePathConsolidated event.
The frozen hand experiment was not rerun or rewritten. It still compiles against the append-only event vocabulary.

Combined with the frozen hand observation that surfaces 10002 and 10001 were delivered but outcome origin 40001 was admitted, the tested core mechanism explains the likely chain: multiple causal origins collapse to the outcome junction identity, that identity is admitted directly, and reverse consolidation stops because the origin is the return source.
All 30 active core tests pass, the two pre-existing adversarial tests remain ignored, and the independently timed warm suite completed in 0.13 seconds, strictly under 10 seconds.
residual_uncertainty: The exact new diagnostic sequence for the frozen hand episode is an inference from immutable prior evidence plus the now-covered core transition; it was intentionally not regenerated. The next ordinary hand development run can capture it directly without another bespoke diagnostic campaign.
Tracing increases returned trace volume only when explicitly enabled; no production trace retention or sampling policy was added.

The receipt covers the current shared dirty worktree, which contains earlier research changes outside this feature; those paths were acknowledged for receipt validation but were not modified by this implementation.
